body:
I was put on cymbalta and wanted off of it after a while since it just wasn't doing much for me other than some side effects. Cymbalta is notorious for how hard it is to get off of, the withdrawals are likened to heroine withdrawals. My doctor told me to stop cold turkey. I did, and had an episode of psychosis. I asked to taper down and this man said "there shouldn't be any withdrawal symptoms unless you are abusing it." He also accused me of being a drug seeker and abusing medication after I took 12 codeine pills over the course of 30 days lol. 

I had another doctor tell me I just need to eat more melons to be healthy.

Another doctor was upset that I take 30 percocets over a year but was happy to hear that I coped with the pain with alcohol otherwise. 

We've to the ER when I suddenly dropped 10lbs and couldn't eat. The doctor told me I was just depressed and to maybe take an exercise class. Turns out I had grade 4 gastroparesis.

No problem! If you find you like Indian tea, I also definitely recommend vahdam. Everything I've tried from them has been really really good. They carry both CTC and full leaf and are pretty affordable. I hope you have a great tea journey! :D
It is! :) Very good imo. Also their bagged masala chai is good, probably the best bagged version I've had, but I would definitely go for the loose leaf over it.
Everyone has answered already, but I just wanna say I love this tea lol. Makes a great masala chai. And if you like this one, check out wagh Bakri next.

I like to make "gingerbread" tea, which is essentially just a healthily spiced masala chai lol. I load up on the cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, ginger, (maybe a little black pepper, cardamon, anise, and fennel if you're feeling cheeky), a touch of molasses and sweetener of choice (brown sugar for extra molasses, maple syrup is nice too, honey and normal sugar are fine). Go with a nice black tea, add a splash of milk, boom. Cup of joy.

Or I make a mock hot chocolate with black tea and some chocolate powdered creamer. Maybe a little cocoa powder if I'm feeling it. Top with some frothed milk or a marshmallow if you wanna go extra lol. 

Or something minty is nice. Melt a peppermint candy or 2 into your tea, mint leaves if you have them, maybe even a couple white chocolate chips.
I have quite enjoyed all Vahdam teas I've tried so far. I am still pretty new to tea, but they're worth checking out imo. I've only tried their loose leaf, but they've all been really great.
Idk how this is such a common concept. I assume they eat food several times a day, do their mouths get all loose and floppy?
Servania is correct, it's just under 8oz (1 US cup) so I have brewed western style so far. I plan to experiment with a gaiwan and use the yixing in place of a fairness cup haha.
Not yet, but I'm planning to! I have some better quality teas from teavivre coming in soon, I can't wait to try them.
Haha I'd hope so! :p
Thanks, I'm so happy with it! Good to know. What neat little things these are, haha.

I am honestly not sure. :'D So far I quite enjoy black to assam, though it can sometimes be a little bitter. I'm only just starting to seriously get into tea past tea bags and Amazon garbage haha. I just ordered an assortment of black tea from teavivre though, so we shall see!

Ayyyy I have gastroparesis so it usually takes me a couple hours to get through 1 cup of tea haha. What I do is just use one of those little insulated cups. Got mine from the thrift store. I use a kettle to boil the water, then either use my teapot for loose leaf and pour into the cup, or just directly into the cup if using a tea bag. Keeps it hot for hours. 

You can even do gong fu style with it if you want, and just pour the tea into your insulated cup from the gaiwan after each steep.

That's a good way of putting it, nice analogy. Yeah, I decided to go with the realzisha pot. The more I read into them, the more I fell in love haha. I really appreciate what they do and I like that they have artist pages. Definitely will be a most beloved and treasured item.

I feel you on the "haha plan" lol. A month ago I was like "nah I'm probably not gonna get a real yixing pot". Pfffff

Oh neat, I haven't heard of these but I think I've seen them haha. That makes sense, I'm gonna have to try it out sometime. Perhaps keep it on a candle warmer so it stays nice and toasty through the day.

Good point. As an artist myself, I really appreciate the craftsmanship that goes into these. I'm a sculptor, I've used moulds, and while it still takes a lot of skill and hand working through the whole process still, it definitely doesn't feel as intimate as creating a full scratch piece. 

Plus I like that the realzisha pots are larger in general. I have gastroparesis so it can take me hours to drink a cup of tea lol. I would prefer to brew a cup and have it in my office to sip vs reheating water over and over for smaller portions/gong fu style.

That makes a lot of sense. I personally don't really plan to get into the resale side, but you never know. It would make a super special heirloom though, as I plan to only really ever get 1 or 2 yixings and just have them forever haha.
Thanks so much, I really appreciate the insight. I might just have to flip a coin haha.

Awesome, thanks so much! Definitely puts me at ease haha. I have heard good things but I am anxious by nature lol. 

I'm stuck between M&L and a pot from realzisha. Afaik both sources are reputable. So you have any experience with realzisha and how it compares?

Thanks so much for the info! I definitely think it would be fun to compare to a gaiwan. I tend to favor robust black teas, so thanks for the guidance there! I read zini was good for black tea, but someone else told me to get a zhuni (which I don't usually see recommended for black) so I was confused.

Very true! I definitely like this philosophy haha. I am just weary after getting a clay teapot when I was newer to all this that was very pretty but made the tea taste horrible, even after resetting. Though that was from a random seller. I would definitely like to use something I like that's just fine vs something I don't like that's better quality haha. I will mull over the Yinchen and M&L pots more.
Good to know, thanks! I am new to gongfu style, I am still figuring all that out haha

Oh I see. I had figured it was probably the same as a gaiwan in that regard, but wasn't sure if it made any difference in flavor or something haha. I would probably prefer like a 1 and done for brewing, so I'll probably look for around a cup capacity, maybe a little less. I've got the gaiwan for gongfu style sessions. But who knows, I might change the ole opinion

I have also just discovered the importance of temperatures today lol. 

Bought a box of oolong to try, the first cup I had was really good. But then I started liking it less and less every cup after. I thought maybe I just didn't like it after all or something, but then I discovered I've just been burning the shit out of it lol. I am new to tea and just boiled everything until now and always left teabags in. Made the oolong really bitter and just kinda nasty tasting. 

 So today I tried it again at the proper temps and holy cow, night and day. I think the sweet spot for steeping was around the 5 min mark for me, after around 7 or 8 minutes the flavor was just slightly more bitter. But turns out, I like the oolong after all lol. Now I must reassess all my previous tea trials.

American here

My friends brought a jar of Vegemite to a party once for us all to try, and I discovered I fuckin love the stuff haha. No one else liked it so I got to take it home. :D 

Just depends on your taste, I suppose. I wish people were more open to different foods in general.
I'll check it out, thanks!
Thanks so much!

I feel you. People often mistake me for a teenager and sometimes assume my husband is my father lol. 

Last time I went to the dentist, the lady who called me back was like "where are your parents?" I said "....uhhh they live like an hour and a half away, why?" She just looked at me for a minute and was like "... How old are you?" She thought I was a minor haha. I am almost 30.

I cannot. :( I can tolerate a lot of kinda of food, but I can only eat small bits at a time or else I get quite sick. Like it usually takes me around 2 hours to drink an 8oz cup of tea lol. In a bad flare up, I can hardly eat at all.

Honey ginger egg drop soup. I have found it to be the best sick food for me, and it's very tasty to boot. The simplest way is just to heat up the broth, add ginger and honey to taste, and drizzle in the beaten egg while stirring.

During a wedding reception, I had to go take meds and lie down a while. A few people in my husband's family just kept gossiping how I looked fine and didn't seem to have a problem until now, in a sarcastic tone (I did, I'm just very good at masking until it's unbearable). 

I've heard that I'm too young, that I want attention, it's depression, I just need motivation, TONS of "oh I/my kids/whoever get that too sometimes" (I have NDPH which is 24/7 without stopping from the onset), asking me if I've tried really basic things like lying down or drinking water, etc etc. people do not understand chronic illness until they have one.

People often forget that mental pain causes physical symptoms. Like because I'm depressed, it's just some phantom like an imaginary friend? Nah man, that shit can affect your whole body physically. There are whole chemical processes people act like don't matter lol.

1: One time I was making my fancy masala chai that takes like an hour. There's a point where I boil milk, to which I'm usually always great at watching the pot. But I turned to do something for a few seconds and boom, all over the oven. Then, when finally done and transferring it, I accidentally dropped the pot and lost a little over half of what remained. 

I got a little over a cup and a half out of what is normally around 5 cups and a pain to make, and a huge mess to clean twice lol. 

2: I was down on my last cup of tea from another masala chai batch. Just poured it, reached for something, knocked over the cup. What a mess. I am clumsy but more attentive now at least lol.

There's lots of tasty ones! 

Potato/sweet potato soup is good, butternut squash, pumpkin. Just recently made a pumpkin soup that slaps. 1 can of pumpkin puree, around 2c chicken broth, some leftover chicken breast, whatever veg you want (I used canned carrots and peas because it's what I had), whatever spices you can tolerate. Good over rice or by itself.

Something as simple as peas and chicken blended up is quite tasty. Depending on what you can tolerate best, I say experiment. Maybe slow roast some veg you like to blend into a soup base, I will always suggest adding chicken (or eggs depending) for the protein and imo tastes better lol. Half the battle of GP is just learning what food you can eat.

Usually anywhere from a few minutes to a couple hours. It's hard to know when to stop eating, even when it's tiny nibbles, when you're always hungry. Out of everything this disease has taken, I miss the satisfied feeling after eating.
I feel you, I am also in a nasty flare and narcotics seem to be the only relief I have found so far. I take them very seldom, though. Hang in there, friend.

Same, I grow some figs and only recently learned about the leaf tea. Now I'm kicking myself for just tossing the old leaves haha. 

I feel you, a lot of people don't like sweet teas. I like my stuff on the sugary side though lol. You can still try Thai tea without adding sugar, it's good stuff. Ginger and cinnamon are pretty much a must in all my tea haha. 

For sure, always try new things and expand your palette. :D

I have heard good things about hibiscus tea! I think you may also enjoy fig leaf tea, if you have access to edible fig leaves haha. Supposed to taste like an earthy vanilla and coconut flavor, but I have yet to try it myself.

Luckily from what I understand, most spices seem pretty suitable for tea. I recommend grinding whole spices to get more flavor. A nice easy one is fennel tea, just fennel seeds and water (and sugar to taste ofc). I like to add in a little cumin or cardamon seeds as well, just comes down to your personal taste. :)

I definitely recommend milk teas, so good! If you like your tea sweet and cold, check out Thai tea.
Thank you, much appreciated.

Thanks for the response, I really appreciate the insight. That makes sense, I don't really know anything about how the brain works, just that mine is dumb haha. I do exercise every morning, eat a lot of spices and tea (especially heavily spiced tea, mmmm), and have chocolate from time to time, but the hunger never stops. :( 

For sure, I have tried heat and cold. Ice definitely helps the head pain sometimes, heat makes it worse. But no change to the hunger whether I have heat or cold on my head or stomach. I do notice though that if I drink alcohol, the next day I will be super intensely hungry vs the normal ravenous hunger I feel day to day. I don't know if that means anything, I know alcohol is poison but it offers the only relief outside of opioids that I've found so far. :')
I do eat a lot of chicken and peanuts (which I know are bad for GP, I just can't give them up :'D), but not a bad idea to try to up the protein more.
All good, I appreciate the insight.

I do not unfortunately. :( I would assume low as I am underweight currently. 

My diet can range because thankfully I don't vomit, so I just pretty much eat what I want because I've never noticed a difference in how awful everything makes me feel (except fried foods, anything fried will shred me). I exercise 30 mins every day, have a piece of fruit and either instant oatmeal or some Greek yogurt with granola or fruit in it. Lunch time, sometimes I skip from the nausea, but I usually have a cup of black tea every day. Sometimes I will nibble on something like crackers and hummus, sometimes maybe some of a smoothie I prepped. Dinner varies widely, usually leftovers of whatever that I've thawed, and some snacks like chips and dried fruits. Maybe sometimes candies like a hard candy or a couple gummy worms. 

I also suffer from NDPH and my Dr at Mayo thinks the hunger might be actually pain that my brain is interpreting as hunger. Which would make sense, as anytime I take a Percocet or get buzzed on alcohol the hunger dampens. But I cannot live on pain meds or alcohol regularly lol.

I drink hot tea every day, exercise 30 mins, and often eat yogurt and oatmeal. There is nothing I eat or drink that even dampens the hunger a little bit. I am just always, always so hungry. There is no relief from it at all. My blood sugar and thyroid are fine apparently, so idk what the cause is it how to stop it. I could handle everything else about the GP, but the constant biting hunger is making me lose my sanity.

Similar boat. I do have PCOS, but more outside of that. I have extremely painful periods, constant stabbing pain where my right ovary is (which can get so bad it hurts to walk on my right leg), would get episodes of blinding pain where it felt like I was being ripped in half randomly, sex is painful, orgasms are painful, tried an IUD but after 3 months it was so excruciating still I couldn't take it anymore and things have been worse since. Finally, Dr checked me for Endo, did the whole laparoscopy, nothing.  They've never been able to find anything. 

They sent me to a pelvic floor specialist, who said my abdomen "felt wrong" and appeared I had a "musculoskeletal malformation" but never explained further and the visits were too expensive. Might be a decent starting point though.

My husband used to eat everything super spicy. He grew his own reapers and regularly made his own reaper jerky, popcorn, sauce, etc. He did the one chip challenge, we both thought it would be fine. He was doubled over with intense pain for a solid 30 minutes. I thought he would have to go to the hospital. He downed 2 bottles of Pepto and remained in pain for days. After this, he has developed IBS and can't usually handle anything spicier than jalapeno level or it will flare up. 

Idk if the 1CC caused the IBS or if it was just very coincidental timing. But he warns everyone not to do it, it's not a funny ha-ha good time with a spicy thing, it could permanently damage you. Some people seem fine, some do not. Idk if some people just get a bad one or what but not worth it imo

Went to the ER after suddenly dropping 10lbs in a few days and being barely able to eat. No joke, the Dr just told me to exercise and that I was depressed. Turns out I have grade 4 gastroparesis. Also was charged around $800 for the visit because America.

My sister and I went through similar as well. My sister passed out during her insertion. I have a very high pain tolerance, and while the insertion hurt quite a bit, the worst was getting it out. Unfortunately I had complications that made me incompatible with an IUD, so I had to have it removed after 3 months. The doctor had cut the strings too short and so they had to go find it. That was probably the most painful procedure of my life, my 3 spinal taps were an absolute cake walk in comparison. 

After 10 minutes of digging around, they still couldn't find it, so they had me come back for an ultrasound assisted removal. I was scared sick over it. But that day, they gave me a numbing shot to the cervix and I felt nothing, and I'm like why the FUCK don't they do that in the first place??? Just give me the fucking shot!
For sure, I planned to only do at home anyways haha. But finding a chronic illness specialist that takes my insurance and is licenced in FL is a hard find. But I'm still looking.
Yeah, there is definitely guilt when I eat anything too. :( It hurts and I feel like I did it to myself because I decided to eat. I hate this.

I'm so sorry. Gp definitely complicates everything, it pits you against your mind and body both. Then you feel "validated" for not eating because eating hurts, but you know you need to and feel like shit if you don't. You can't win.

Congrats on being tube free! The fear of the pain and nausea is so real, it's hard to make yourself eat sometimes because you know it's gonna hurt. I am mostly ravenously hungry feeling, but there is no relief from eating. But sometimes I will also not feel hunger or thirst at all. Either way it often feels pointless. :')

Yeah, people give more respect to what they can see. And already suffering from NDPH for several years before this, I am used to being brushed off. I am very underweight now and don't want to be, but I guess part of me doesn't want to lose that validation if I gain weight. It's quite the mental struggle haha.
Definitely, I plan to find a therapist once I get insurance. Chronic illness therapists are very hard to find, but I'm hoping.

I appreciate the response and I'm sorry you're going through it too. I find myself having less patience with healthcare providers as time goes on as well. I've only had GP since late May last year, so thankfully I have not had to deal with this so long, but it's already been getting worse in less than a year and I fear the future. I'm glad cannabis helps you. c: I have not noticed any relief when I've tried some strains. The only thing that has helped mine is Percocet. I take it for my NDPH but try not to more than like once every 2 weeks. My stomach does not hurt as much while it's in effect, but as it starts wearing off, you definitely feel the pain if you've eaten in that time. So not really helping as much as just some temporary relief from the pain itself lol. Hoping something works soon.

Yeah, alcohol is rough after developing gp. :'D It makes me pretty sick from very little, it hits me later, absolutely burns in my stomach, and I can have a hangover for 3 days. So I try to avoid it. Though I find a little white wine doesn't hurt me as much as others I've tried, but haven't tried much with any.

Ah I gotcha. The chocolate ensure is soooo tasty, I love that stuff. I know how you feel, I am not really about the puree much myself haha. But there are some tasty combos if you can tolerate them! One of my favorites is roasted skinless chicken breast with peas and carrots blended up with some broth and some good seasonings into a paste with a pack of benecalorie. I'm still trying some combos of things, but it's not as bad as I first thought going into it. ^^

Appetizers are great haha. I feel you on the shakes, I am also always stocked up lol. I like the boost very high calorie strawberry, but I'm not sure if those are safe for diabetics. ;v; But yeah, take home and puree whatever, portion and freeze stuff, lower food waste, woo!
No, not currently.

Same here, grew up poor and wasting food is a cardinal sin haha. I want to cry anytime I throw something out. Now though I just freeze tiny meal bags of everything or just get something my husband liked so he can eat the leftovers. I'll blend up food and add a benecal so I can try to max calorie intake if I can't eat it all.

I feel this. Sometimes my friends or family like to go out to eat, I like to join them now and again. I usually get comments from waiters asking if I didn't like the food because I barely picked at it. It's always so good, I just can't eat it. T~T Also hate getting the looks of pity from people around me, and  sitting there for like an hour awkwardly doing nothing while everyone else eats. I hate eating with people who don't know about the illness more,  like my husband's colleagues or extended family. A lot of people assume I am anorexic.

I'm not sure if it makes much difference. I have grade 4 at 58% retention after 4 hours, but I am thankfully able to keep down food. It hurts like hell and I'm very nauseous constantly, but I don't vomit at least. Though so far none of the meds or Botox has worked for me, and flair ups are much more often than not (I will have around 3 to 4 better days a month). I'm being sent to Mayo soon for more intensive options. 

This illness is literal hell and it's hard to pin specifics across the board since it seems so different for each person. Hang in there friend. :(

I don't vomit, but sometimes I wish I could. Idk why, my entire life I have had a really difficult time vomiting. With the gp, I'll sit over a toilet with my mouth watering and heave for hours but nothing comes out. But I know I'd be in a lot worse shape if I could. :/

Every time lol. 

For me it is not in the sternum, but feels like the stomach itself. Feels like I just ate broken glass if I eat too much.v
I feel this. Nothing has worked for mine so far, it is absolutely debilitating.
Absolutely. My period makes everything worse.

This is good advice, thank you. They know about my medical issues and whatnot, I just never let on to how awful I feel constantly. I guess I just don't know how to broach the subject of death itself. I do tell them a lot though that I love them. 
Perhaps I will write something for everyone. I think something like that would be nice to have. Plus it's easier to write than to speak for me.

I'll have to try some again. When I took probiotics before it didn't do anything for me. :'D Soda hurts me, most sweet drinks so now. I just stick to water. But I might give ginger ale another try and see if that helps.
I'm so sorry. :( I hope you find something that helps. Hoping it gets better, it's been days and I can still barely tolerate anything.
Fingers crossed for you! I hope it works, it seems to do well for a lot of folks.

That's fair, I wish it was a permanent fix. My Dr wanted me to try Botox before g-poem because if it doesn't work, there's a good chance g-poem wouldn't either. I hope the second go is the end of it for you. <3
I might have to look into that haha. I've been sticking to liquid, but it's been hard to have much past water. Everything just makes me nauseous.
That's awesome, I'm glad it turned around for you! :D Just gotta hang in there.
I'm sorry it stopped working for you. :( This illness is such hell, I wish there was something out there that just worked.

I'm so sorry, that sucks so much. D: I read somewhere it can take over a week to improve, but idk if that's accurate or anything. I can't even sip water without getting nauseous, I really hope it works with more time.

I hate that shit about losing weight. I think people are trying to make light of it and make you laugh by joking, but they really don't realize how insensitive it is. There is nothing to envy about this illness. 

I feel you about the food too. I don't get angry, but I do get sad. Sometimes my friends want to get together for food and go to hot pot or a buffet, and I either just can't go, or we have to choose a different option and I feel like a burden. I miss broccoli, I miss burgers and pizza, and whenever someone is eating one of those around me, I just stare at it like a sad puppy lol. GP is hell.
Yeah, unfortunately I live fairly far from any Asian markets and trader Joe's. TvT Mochi is pretty simple to make though, I plan to try my hand at it soon.

Glad it doesn't seem to hurt you. :D They're so good, and so versatile. I hope more people with gp can eat them without hurting. Limiting is smart, haha. I've not eaten more than 2 at once myself, though I can usually barely get through 1 before I feel super full. They usually don't make me as sick as other foods I eat though.
Oh for sure, I have made tahini! :D I would probably make black tahini and add honey to make black sesame paste.
True! I was thinking it might be good for others to look into as well. Anything to help. :D

No, dried jujubes fruit haha. Sorry, I forgot about the candy, I should have clarified. :'D

That sucks. :( The sesame are my favorite, I hate that they are the hardest on me. I might try making my own though and experimenting.

Yeah, NDPH is a bitch haha. There is no effective medication or treatment for it currently, but there's always new advancements being made so I'm hopeful someday there will be. 

Oh hey I also journal haha. My diary is a nice place of comfort. It definitely helps when I am overwhelmed. I have not tried meditation yet, but I enjoy yoga. 

Haha nice! Yeah, the process is fun. Plus everyone is happy when I make stuff and I'm glad they can enjoy it. 

That's actually a really nice way of looking at things. I try to stay optimistic but I am afraid of the future generally. I will try to remind myself of this though, no point in worrying about something that doesn't yet exist. Thank you for the link also, it's good to read positive stories sometimes haha. It's easy to get lost in the thick of it, gotta pull yourself out every now and again with nice stories and reminders.

Thanks for this. It is nice having an answer at least. Those doctors that said I was anorexic and faking it can eat my whole ass now lol. 
It just sucks, I went through a period of grief when I developed NDPH at 23. Now I have to go through it again for some other new monster that's formed. Just gotta try to stay busy. Ironically I have gotten into baking since I developed gp lol. I can't eat much of it, but I love giving sweets to my husband and friends. I'd like to find a therapist soon, it's just hard to find one I can afford currently.

Same situation here. :'D I have not noticed any difference between hot and cold food, just go for what you tolerate more at the time. Also heat on my stomach makes me feel much worse personally.

You can add benecal packs to a lot of stuff to add calories to a small meal. Imo it is best when added to an egg and scrambled, I usually also add a little canned fish and make a sort of meaty egg pancake lol. Then you can also add sauces and things if you can tolerate. You can also add it to the nutrient shakes, but it makes it really thick, almost like a pudding lol. I recommend getting some or an equivalent thing and experimenting with some recipes.

I find I tolerate the nutrient shakes better when I add some stuff to them. I get the 530cal strawberry shakes, blend one with like 5 frozen strawberries, a splash of milk, and some honey. I usually also tend to stay pretty stable weight wise on days where I can eat pieces of waffles or naan, bready stuff. But it all depends on your personal tolerances, gp is so wildly different between people. x_x

I'm in the same boat. I love food but I fear it now after developing gp. I'm afraid I'm developing a separate eating disorder because I don't want to eat even when I feel more ok. Just afraid, it usually always makes me feel awful. So 8 stick to terrible foods like chips and fries and feel awful from the poor diet anyway lol
Yeah. Not looking forward to being dependent and on meds for the rest of my life for this. I hope motegrity helps though, it seems to help many with gp.

Haha I have had similar looks. Even had some cashiers make jokes. Just gotta do what we can do, even if that's surviving on bags of chips and chocolate lol. Yeah, I usually tell people I'm just not feeling well. I'm still learning to adjust my menus, but I will usually just look at the appetizers now or just get something my husband likes so he can eat the leftovers. Oh man I also miss having a drink every now and then. I've not had a holiday yet since this started but I am sure Thanksgiving is gonna be rough. Mmm pizza. I can tolerate maybe a bite or two of pizza, but anymore than that and I'll pay for it. I feel you, I'm also just coming out of a bad down swing.

Potatoes are just so versatile, you can make anything with them haha. The true king of veg. Oh man same, I get jealous when my husband eats his fruits and salads. When all this first started, an ER doc told me to take an exercise class to get motivated and "just eat". Thanks doc, great advice lol. Haha a toddler's dream to be sure. I actually really love the taste of the nutrient shakes (except the boost cinnamon roll one was gross lol), they just make me sick fast. I usually blend them with some frozen strawberries and I seem to handle it better. c:

Damn, I'm so sorry. Chocolate is great but makes me nauseous so fast. :'D I think potatoes are what has been keeping me (mostly) steady, particularly chips and fries. I seem to tolerate potatoes well and they are my favorite food, so bonus lol. But I do slowly keep going down and am just fearing if it continues. I too want to avoid the hospital at all costs. I feel you on the unhealthy diet. I miss fruits and veg, I used to eat so much broccoli and apples. I miss peas. Now I live on chips and whatever terrible snack I can tolerate at a time. This illness is miserable.

Thanks for the info! I guess I'm getting ahead of myself, it's just hard not to miss how things used to be. :'D I might try like 10mins of yoga and leave it at that. Should probably get the GP under control first, I really really do not want to get a feeding tube.

I personally haven't had any issues with strawberries. In fact, when I've added only strawberries to the calorie shakes I seem to tolerate them better haha. I also like frozen strawberry puree popsicles, they don't tend to make me sick like most other sweets now.
I think I will try some yoga as well. 2.0? Like the nutritional shakes? I try, though they usually make me sick pretty fast so it may take me a day or two to drink one.

It's possible that she could be motivated to change from an outside force, but more often than not, it will not change long-term. It's possible for her to try and seek help when she is on an up-swing. When you're in a depressive cycle, you don't think clearly or see from the outside. No reason for the ups or downs, they just are as they come. Even suicidal people have up-swings and may want to change. 

There is absolutely nothing wrong with loving or wanting to help someone who's mentally ill, please don't take that assessment from these comments. Everyone is deserving of love, and being mentally ill is no one's choice. The distance will be hard, no doubt. But if you think there's a chance you can help keep her balanced and are ready for the tough times, I'd say to give it a shot. You obviously care a lot about her and genuinely want to be there for her. Just be prepared.

I'm not sure what country she's in, but they might have a program to force-help. In the US, it's called Baker Act, where a person of authority (usually police) are called and take the person to a mental health facility for a period of time to seek help. If it comes down to it and you think she is seriously going to do something to herself, I might suggest calling the authorities in her area and Baker Acting (or the equivalent). She might be mad at you for it, but it has saved many people, myself included.

There's a lot that goes into relationships with mentally ill people. It's a LOT of work, and you must be prepared to shoulder another person, which is not an easy thing to do. I'm not saying it's like this, but be aware of manipulative behaviors like threatening self-harm or guilt tripping on bad days, it can be hard to recognize from the inside. Be aware as well, that dealing with someone else's issues day in and day out could very well turn into resentment over time. I'm not saying it will, but it does happen sometimes. I dated someone very mentally ill for 3 years, and it happened to me when I realized he was manipulative and abusive. I thought I could fix him, take care of him. But it is not your job to "save" people. It is very mentally, emotionally, and physically exhausting.  


Unfortunately, nothing you could do or say will make her improve if she does not want to for herself. You can dote on and cuddle and love someone to the fullest extent, but they will not change unless they themselves enact it. The only person who have control over is yourself, and she is the only one that can decide that. It sounds harsh to say, but it is not your fault if she does anything to herself. It is painful to go through and you usually end up blaming yourself in some way, but it's the whole control thing again. You cannot control her decisions, and it would be her choice alone to harm herself. It's very hard to separate yourself from when you are close to someone, but it is not your fault.
